title: Biology Unit 1: Acellular Life — MCQ Question Bank

questions.question: Which feature best distinguishes viruses from typical cellular organisms?

options.A: They contain genetic material

questions.question: The genetic material of a virus may consist of:

options.A: DNA only
options.D: Both DNA and RNA in every virus

questions.question: A virus that specifically infects bacteria is called a:

options.A: Viroid

questions.question: The protein coat surrounding viral genetic material is called the:

options.A: Capsule

questions.question: HIV primarily targets cells involved in:

options.A: Oxygen transport

questions.question: AIDS is caused by infection with:

options.A: HBV

questions.question: Which is a recognized route of HIV transmission?

options.A: Sharing classroom air

questions.question: A virus containing RNA as its genetic material is classified, at the basic level, as:

options.A: A DNA virus

questions.question: Viruses are generally described as acellular because they:

options.A: Have no nucleic acid

questions.question: Which pairing is correctly matched?

options.A: HIV — AIDS

questions.question: A virus with a lipid layer surrounding its capsid is described as:

options.A: Naked

questions.question: Why does a virus depend on a host cell for multiplication?

options.A: It has no genetic material

questions.question: Which information is especially useful when classifying a virus?

options.A: Patient's favorite food
options.C: Weather on the day of infection

questions.question: Which statement about HIV and AIDS is correct?

options.A: HIV and AIDS are exactly the same term
options.B: HIV infection can progress to AIDS
options.D: AIDS is transmitted by casual contact

questions.question: Which statement about viral genomes is correct?

options.A: Every virus has both DNA and RNA
options.D: A viral genome may be DNA or RNA

questions.question: Virus A has RNA and Virus B has DNA. What can be concluded directly?

options.A: Virus A must be larger
options.B: They differ in type of genetic material

questions.question: A person exposed to HIV has no immediate obvious symptoms. What is the safest conclusion?

options.A: HIV infection is impossible
options.B: Lack of immediate symptoms alone does not rule out infection
options.C: HIV always causes immediate severe illness

questions.question: Two viruses have similar capsids but different nucleic acids. Which feature most clearly separates them genetically?

options.A: Capsid color

questions.question: A newly discovered virus is being classified. Which combination is most informative?

options.A: Host, genome type, structure and associated disease

questions.question: Why is it incorrect to say that viruses have no genetic information?

options.A: They are made only of lipids
options.B: Their nucleic acid carries genetic information
options.C: Host cells destroy all viral genes

questions.question: Which structure directly encloses the viral genome in a typical non-enveloped virus?

options.A: Capsid

questions.question: A bacteriophage is best defined as a virus that:

options.A: Infects plants only

questions.question: Which statement best describes a virus outside a suitable host cell?

options.A: It performs complete cellular metabolism
options.B: It exists as a non-cellular infectious particle

questions.question: Which characteristic can be used to distinguish viruses from one another?

options.A: Genome type

questions.question: If a virus has RNA rather than DNA, which conclusion is justified?

options.A: It is an RNA virus

questions.question: Which statement about viral replication is most accurate?

options.A: Viruses normally reproduce independently in nutrient broth
options.B: Viruses use host-cell systems to produce new viral components
options.D: Viruses always divide into two equal cells

questions.question: Which feature is NOT a typical basis for viral classification in the stated learning outcome?

options.A: Genetic material

questions.question: Which is the best example of a host-specific viral relationship?

options.A: A bacteriophage infecting a bacterium
options.B: A virus forming a plant root
options.C: A virus becoming a red blood cell

questions.question: A virus contains a protein capsid but no cellular cytoplasm. This supports the idea that it is:

options.A: A complete cell

questions.question: Which statement about the viral capsid is correct?

options.A: It is a protein covering associated with the viral genome
options.B: It is the host cell's nucleus
options.C: It is always made of DNA
options.D: It is a bacterial cell wall

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares a virus with a typical cell?

options.A: Both always carry out independent metabolism
options.B: A virus lacks the complete cellular organization of a typical cell
options.D: A virus always has a nucleus

questions.question: Which observation would support classification of a virus as an RNA virus?

options.A: Detection of RNA as its genome

questions.question: Which statement is most appropriate regarding viral disease?

options.A: Every virus causes the same disease
options.B: Different viruses can be associated with different diseases and hosts
options.D: Disease type determines whether a virus has DNA or RNA in every case

questions.question: HIV is relevant to the study of acellular life because HIV is:

options.A: A cellular bacterium

questions.question: Which event represents a recognized form of HIV transmission?

options.A: Sharing infected blood through contaminated equipment

questions.question: Which statement about AIDS is most accurate?

options.A: It refers to a condition associated with advanced HIV infection
options.B: It is a type of bacterium
options.C: It is a form of influenza
options.D: It is transmitted by ordinary air

questions.question: A student says, “If a virus has a capsid, it must be a cellular organism.” What is the best correction?

options.A: Capsids are found only in bacteria
options.B: A capsid is a viral structure and does not make the virus a cell

questions.question: Which combination can provide useful evidence for identifying a virus?

options.A: Genome type and host range

questions.question: Why can two viruses with different genomes still belong to the same broad biological group?

options.A: Genome type is only one feature used to describe viruses
options.D: Genome type has no biological significance

questions.question: Which statement is correct about viral genetic material?

options.A: It is always DNA
options.C: It can be DNA or RNA depending on the virus
options.D: It is always both DNA and RNA

questions.question: Which feature most directly indicates that a virus is enveloped?

options.A: A lipid membrane-like outer layer
options.B: Presence of a bacterial cell wall

questions.question: A virus infects bacteria but contains RNA. Which two features can be used together in its description?

options.A: Host and genome type

questions.question: Which statement about viral host range is most reasonable?

options.A: Every virus can infect every organism
options.B: Viruses may show specificity for particular hosts or cell types
options.D: Host has no relevance to viral classification

questions.question: Which statement best explains why viruses are not treated as ordinary cells?

options.A: They have no genetic material
options.B: They do not possess the complete organization and independent machinery of cells
options.C: They are always visible to the naked eye

questions.question: Which feature can be used to compare two viruses structurally?

options.A: Capsid and presence or absence of an envelope

questions.question: A scientist detects viral RNA inside an infected host cell. What is the most direct classification statement?

options.A: The virus has an RNA genome
options.B: The virus must be a bacterium
options.D: The virus must lack a capsid

questions.question: Which statement about HIV transmission is correct?

options.A: HIV spreads through ordinary handshakes
options.B: HIV can be transmitted through infected blood
options.C: HIV is routinely spread by sharing air
options.D: HIV is spread by casual classroom contact

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes HIV from AIDS?

options.A: HIV is the virus; AIDS is a syndrome/advanced condition associated with HIV infection
options.B: HIV is a bacterium; AIDS is a virus
options.C: HIV is a symptom; AIDS is a blood cell

questions.question: A researcher wants to compare two viruses. Which data would be least useful for the biological classification described?

options.A: Genome type

questions.question: A virus has a capsid and an envelope. Which conclusion is justified?

options.A: It has two complete cells
options.B: It is an enveloped virus particle
options.C: It must contain both DNA and RNA

questions.question: Which statement about viral multiplication is correct?

options.A: Host-cell machinery can be used to make viral components
options.D: Viruses contain all organelles needed for independent life

questions.question: If two viruses infect different hosts, host information can help:

options.A: Classify or distinguish them

questions.question: Which of the following is a structural feature of many viruses?

options.A: Capsid
options.D: Ribosome as a complete cellular organelle

questions.question: Which statement is scientifically safest about symptoms following HIV exposure?

options.A: Symptoms alone can never be interpreted without testing and clinical context
options.B: Immediate absence of symptoms proves no infection
options.C: Every infected person develops AIDS immediately

questions.question: A student classifies viruses only by the disease they cause. Why is this incomplete?

options.A: Viral classification can also consider genome and structural features and host
options.B: Disease is never related to viruses

questions.question: Which pair contains one virus-related term and its correct description?

options.A: Capsid — protein coat associated with a viral particle

questions.question: Which conclusion follows from finding DNA as a viral genome?

options.A: The virus is a DNA virus

questions.question: Which conclusion follows from finding RNA as a viral genome?

options.A: The virus is an RNA virus

questions.question: Which statement about an acellular infectious particle is most consistent with the concept of a virus?

options.A: It lacks the complete organization of a cell

questions.question: Which combination gives the strongest basic description of an unknown virus?

options.A: Genome type, structural features, host and associated disease

questions.question: A virus has no envelope but has a capsid. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

options.A: It is a non-enveloped virus particle
options.D: It must have both DNA and RNA

questions.question: Why is host information useful in viral classification?

options.A: Viruses can have different host associations

questions.question: Which statement best links viral structure and function?

options.A: The capsid is associated with protection and packaging of viral genetic material
options.D: The capsid is the host's nucleus

questions.question: Which statement about HIV is correct?

options.A: HIV is a virus that can damage the immune system
options.B: HIV is a bacterium that causes malaria

questions.question: Which is NOT a recognized casual route of HIV transmission?

options.A: Ordinary handshake
options.D: Transmission from an infected mother to child under relevant circumstances

questions.question: A virus contains genetic material but no cytoplasm. What does this observation support?

options.A: Viral particles do not have the complete organization of typical cells

questions.question: Which evidence would be most useful for distinguishing a DNA virus from an RNA virus?

options.A: Type of nucleic acid in its genome

questions.question: A researcher knows only that a particle causes disease. Why is more information needed before classifying it as a virus?

options.A: Disease alone does not establish genome and structural identity

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between HIV and AIDS?

options.A: HIV infection can lead to AIDS, but the terms do not mean the same thing
options.C: HIV is a symptom of AIDS
options.D: HIV and AIDS are two unrelated bacteria

questions.question: A new viral isolate has RNA, a capsid, an envelope, and a human host. Which set of observations is most useful for its classification?

options.A: Genome type, structure and host

questions.question: Which statement best explains why a virus is called acellular?

options.A: It has no genetic material
options.B: It is not organized as a complete cell

questions.question: Which combination can be used to classify a virus according to the stated learning outcomes?

options.A: Genome type, structure, host and disease association
options.C: Weather, location and time of day

questions.question: A virus contains DNA as its genetic material. Which statement follows directly?

options.A: It is a DNA virus

questions.question: A virus contains RNA as its genetic material. Which statement does NOT necessarily follow?

options.A: It is an RNA virus
options.D: It may have structural features that distinguish it from other RNA viruses

questions.question: Which structure is most directly associated with the protein component surrounding viral genetic material?

options.A: Capsid

questions.question: What is a major difference between a virus and a typical cellular organism?

options.A: A virus lacks complete independent cellular machinery
options.B: A virus never contains nucleic acid
options.C: A virus cannot interact with living cells
options.D: A virus is always made of carbohydrates

questions.question: Which statement about bacteriophages is correct?

options.A: They are viruses that infect bacteria
options.B: They are bacteria that infect viruses

questions.question: If two viruses have different host organisms, host association can be:

options.A: Useful information for distinguishing them

questions.question: Which statement about viral replication is most appropriate?

options.A: Viruses rely on a suitable host cell to produce new viral particles
options.B: Viruses always reproduce by binary fission
options.D: Viruses produce all required cellular organelles independently

questions.question: Which observation most strongly supports the identification of a viral particle rather than a typical cell?

options.A: It has a viral genome and capsid but lacks complete cellular organization
options.B: It has a nucleus and mitochondria

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a viral genome?

options.A: It is genetic material carried by the virus
options.B: It is always located in a nucleus

questions.question: Which feature can vary among viruses?

options.A: Type of genome

questions.question: A researcher finds a virus with a lipid envelope. Which conclusion is justified?

options.A: It is an enveloped virus

questions.question: Which statement about viral envelopes is most appropriate?

options.A: An envelope is an outer lipid-containing layer found in some viruses
options.C: An envelope is a bacterial chromosome
options.D: An envelope is the same as a nucleus

questions.question: Which feature would be most useful in comparing the genetic classification of two viruses?

options.A: Their nucleic acid type

questions.question: A virus infects humans and contains RNA. Which conclusion is justified?

options.A: It is an RNA virus associated with a human host

questions.question: Which statement about disease association is correct?

options.A: Viruses can be associated with different diseases
options.C: Every virus causes the same disease

questions.question: A student says, “All RNA viruses cause the same disease.” What is the best response?

options.A: Incorrect; RNA viruses can differ in hosts, structures and disease associations
options.C: Correct; all RNA viruses are HIV
options.D: Incorrect because RNA viruses do not exist

questions.question: Which information would be least relevant to basic viral classification?

options.A: Patient's favorite subject

questions.question: A virus is found to infect bacteria. Which term should be considered?

options.A: Bacteriophage

questions.question: Which statement about viruses and cells is correct?

options.A: Viruses do not possess the full range of structures required for independent cellular life

questions.question: Why can a virus have genetic material even though it is acellular?

options.A: Genetic material does not by itself make a particle a complete cell
options.B: Only cells can contain genetic information
options.C: Viral genetic material is actually host DNA in every case

questions.question: Which statement best connects host dependence and viral replication?

options.A: A host cell provides machinery and conditions needed for viral multiplication
options.B: Host cells prevent every virus from reproducing
options.C: Viruses make all cellular machinery before entering a host

questions.question: A researcher records genome type, capsid structure, envelope status and host. Why is this useful?

options.A: These observations provide multiple features for viral classification
options.B: These observations determine the patient's personality
options.C: These observations prove all viruses are identical
options.D: These observations eliminate the need to study the genome

questions.question: Which statement about HIV is correct?

options.A: HIV is the virus associated with AIDS
options.B: HIV is a type of red blood cell

questions.question: Which route can transmit HIV?

options.A: Contact with infected blood
options.D: Sitting next to an infected person

questions.question: Which statement about casual contact with a person living with HIV is correct?

options.A: Ordinary handshaking is not a recognized route of HIV transmission
options.C: Sharing a classroom always transmits HIV

questions.question: Which statement best describes AIDS in relation to HIV?

options.A: AIDS is an advanced syndrome associated with HIV infection
options.C: AIDS is the capsid of HIV
options.D: AIDS is a type of viral genome

questions.question: Which statement is scientifically appropriate about symptoms of HIV infection?

options.A: Symptoms can vary and absence of immediate symptoms does not by itself rule out infection
options.C: No infected person ever has symptoms
options.D: Symptoms always identify HIV with certainty

questions.question: Which factor is important when considering HIV transmission?

options.A: The type of exposure and whether it involves infected body fluids
options.B: The color of the person's clothes

questions.question: A student claims HIV can be transmitted by a normal handshake. Which response is correct?

options.A: A normal handshake is not a recognized route of HIV transmission

questions.question: Which statement about HIV and the immune system is correct?

options.A: HIV targets cells important to immune function
options.C: HIV directly becomes a red blood cell

questions.question: Which observation would best support that an unknown infectious particle is a virus?

options.A: It contains viral genetic material and shows viral structural organization
options.B: It contains a complete nucleus and mitochondria

questions.question: Which statement about viral classification is most complete?

options.A: Classification can consider genome type, structure, host and disease association
options.C: Classification depends only on patient age

questions.question: Two viruses have the same host but different genome types. What can be concluded?

options.A: Genome type can still distinguish them
options.C: They must cause the same disease

questions.question: Two viruses have the same genome type but different hosts. Which statement is valid?

options.A: Host association can provide another distinguishing characteristic
options.B: They must be the same virus

questions.question: Which statement about capsids is most appropriate?

options.A: Capsids are protein structures associated with viral particles
options.D: Capsids are always made of RNA

questions.question: A viral particle has a capsid but no envelope. Which description is suitable?

options.A: Non-enveloped or naked virus particle

questions.question: Which conclusion is NOT justified from knowing only that a virus is enveloped?

options.A: It contains DNA rather than RNA
options.C: It has a viral structural feature
options.D: It may also have a capsid

questions.question: A scientist wants to distinguish two viruses with identical hosts. Which additional information is especially useful?

options.A: Genome and structural features

questions.question: Which statement about viral genomes is correct?

options.A: Viral genomes carry information needed for viral reproduction and functions
options.B: Viral genomes have no biological role
options.C: Viral genomes are always host chromosomes

questions.question: A student says, “Because viruses need host cells, they have no genes.” What is wrong with this statement?

options.A: Host dependence does not mean absence of viral genetic information
options.B: Viruses are made only of genes

questions.question: Which feature is most directly related to the term “host” in virology?

options.A: The organism or cell that a virus infects

questions.question: Which statement about host specificity is reasonable?

options.A: Different viruses may have different host associations
options.B: Every virus has exactly the same host

questions.question: Which combination best represents structural information about a virus?

options.A: Capsid and envelope status

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between a virus and its host cell?

options.A: The virus uses host-cell processes to produce viral components
options.B: The virus permanently becomes the host cell
options.C: The host cell becomes a bacterium
options.D: The virus produces a complete independent organism before entering the cell

questions.question: Which statement about HIV transmission is correct?

options.A: Certain infected body-fluid exposures can transmit HIV
options.D: Mosquito bites are the recognized routine route

questions.question: Which statement is correct about HIV and mosquitoes?

options.A: Mosquito bites are not a recognized route of HIV transmission
options.C: HIV multiplies in mosquitoes and causes AIDS

questions.question: Which statement best describes the cause of AIDS?

options.A: AIDS is associated with HIV infection
options.B: AIDS is caused by ordinary bacteria
options.C: AIDS is caused by lack of oxygen alone
options.D: AIDS is caused by a capsid

questions.question: A person wants to know whether HIV infection is present. Which is the most appropriate general approach?

options.A: Appropriate medical testing and professional evaluation
options.D: Asking whether the person shook hands

questions.question: Which statement about appearance and HIV is correct?

options.A: Appearance alone cannot reliably establish whether someone has HIV
options.B: HIV can always be diagnosed by looking at a person
options.C: AIDS always has a unique visible appearance

questions.question: Which statement about symptoms is most scientifically appropriate?

options.A: Symptoms alone are not a reliable substitute for appropriate HIV testing
options.C: Absence of symptoms proves no infection

questions.question: Which information would best help classify an unknown virus under the stated learning outcome?

options.A: Genome type, structural features, host and associated disease

questions.question: A virus is found to contain RNA and a capsid but no envelope. Which description is best?

options.A: An RNA, non-enveloped virus particle
options.C: A DNA virus with an envelope

questions.question: A virus contains DNA and an envelope. Which statement is justified?

options.A: It is a DNA virus with an envelope

questions.question: Which statement best illustrates why multiple characteristics are useful in viral classification?

options.A: One feature alone may not fully describe differences among viruses

questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?

options.A: Capsid — viral protein coat

questions.question: Which statement about an enveloped virus is correct?

options.A: The envelope is an outer layer associated with some viral particles
options.C: The envelope is the same as the capsid
options.D: The envelope is a host-cell nucleus

questions.question: Which statement about viral structure is correct?

options.A: Structural features can contribute to viral classification
options.B: Structure has no relation to classification
options.D: Viruses always have the same envelope

questions.question: A virus is discovered in a bacterial culture. Which possibility should be considered first?

options.A: It may be a bacteriophage
options.B: It must be a human cell

questions.question: Which statement is most consistent with the concept of acellular life?

options.A: Viral particles are not complete cells but can contain genetic information
options.B: Every acellular particle is a bacterium

questions.question: Which feature separates an RNA virus from a DNA virus most directly?

options.A: The chemical type of its genome

questions.question: Which statement about viral diseases is correct?

options.A: Disease association can provide useful information when studying a virus
options.B: Every virus causes the same disease
options.C: Disease association is impossible to observe
options.D: Viruses are never associated with disease

questions.question: A researcher knows a virus causes disease but does not know its genome. What additional information would be valuable?

options.A: Genome type and structural features

questions.question: Which statement about HIV infection is correct?

options.A: HIV can affect the immune system
options.B: HIV is a normal human chromosome

questions.question: Which statement is correct regarding transmission from mother to child?

options.A: HIV can be transmitted from an infected mother to child under relevant circumstances
options.B: HIV can never pass from mother to child
options.C: HIV transmission occurs only through handshakes
options.D: Mother-to-child transmission is caused by mosquito bites

questions.question: Which statement best explains why “no immediate symptoms” is not enough to rule out HIV?

options.A: Infection status cannot be established from immediate symptoms alone
options.C: Symptoms have no relation to infection at all
options.D: Every exposed person automatically has AIDS

questions.question:
A student compares Virus A and Virus B:
Virus A: RNA genome, human host.
Virus B: DNA genome, bacterial host.
Which comparison uses two relevant classification features?

options.A: Genome type and host

questions.question: A virus has a capsid, an RNA genome and a human host. Which statement is most defensible?

options.A: It can be described using structural, genetic and host characteristics

questions.question: Which overall statement best summarizes Unit 1?

options.A: Viruses are acellular infectious particles whose classification can involve genome, structure, host and disease; HIV is associated with AIDS
options.B: All viruses are bacteria and all diseases are caused by viruses
options.C: Viruses have complete cellular machinery and reproduce independently
options.D: HIV is transmitted through ordinary social contact
